records.literal_gloss: And were finished the heavens and the earth and all their host.

en.L: And the heavens and the earth were finished, and all their host.
en.B: So the heavens and the earth were completed, with everything in them.
en.R: So God finished making the heavens and the earth and everything in them.

es.L: Y fueron terminados los cielos y la tierra, y todo su ejército.
es.B: Así quedaron terminados los cielos y la tierra, con todo lo que hay en ellos.
es.R: Así terminó Dios de hacer el cielo y la tierra y todo lo que hay en ellos.

fr.L: Et les cieux et la terre furent achevés, ainsi que toute leur armée.
fr.B: Ainsi furent menés à leur terme les cieux et la terre, avec tout ce qu’ils contiennent.
fr.R: Ainsi, Dieu a fini de faire le ciel et la terre, et tout ce qui s’y trouve.

sw.L: Na mbingu na dunia zikakamilishwa, na jeshi lao lote.
sw.B: Hivyo mbingu na dunia zikakamilika, pamoja na vyote vilivyomo.
sw.R: Basi Mungu akamaliza kufanya mbingu na dunia na kila kitu kilichomo.

vi.L: Và trời và đất đã được hoàn tất, cùng mọi vạn vật của chúng.
vi.B: Vậy trời và đất đã được hoàn tất, cùng với mọi vật ở trong đó.
vi.R: Vậy Đức Chúa Trời đã làm xong trời và đất, cùng với mọi vật ở trong đó.

ko.L: 그리고 하늘과 땅과 그 모든 무리가 다 이루어졌다.
ko.B: 이렇게 하늘과 땅과 그 안의 모든 것이 다 완성되었다.
ko.R: 이렇게 하나님께서는 하늘과 땅과 그 안에 있는 모든 것을 다 만드셨다.

decisions.choice: all their host: everything that fills them
decisions.reason: The word means an army, or any great ordered company. Here it gathers up everything that fills the heavens and the earth: the lights and stars of the sky (Deuteronomy 4:19 calls them "the host of heaven") and all that lives on the earth.

decisions.choice: were finished: God finished them
decisions.reason: The passive does not say who finished them, but verse 2 does: God completed his work. The verb means brought to completion, with nothing lacking.

decisions.choice: 2:1-3 closes the account of the seven days
alternatives: the start of a new section with chapter 2
decisions.reason: Chapter divisions were added to the Bible in the Middle Ages. These three verses belong with chapter 1: they close the account of the seven days, and "the heavens and the earth" recalls its first verse. In the Hebrew manuscripts the paragraph break comes after verse 3.

decisions.choice: God finished making
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who finished, as verse 2 does (m2).

decisions.choice: todo su ejército
decisions.reason: Spanish has no word that, like English "host", can mean both an army and a great company. Literal keeps "ejército", the word's plain sense; meaning decision m1 says what it covers. Balanced and Readable say "todo lo que hay en ellos".

decisions.choice: passé simple at Literal and Balanced ("furent achevés", "se reposa"); passé composé at Readable ("a fini", "s'est reposé")
decisions.reason: The tense choice for French narrative in Genesis, recorded in 1:1: the passé simple of written narrative at Literal and Balanced, the passé composé of spoken French at Readable.

decisions.choice: "mọi vạn vật của chúng" (L), "mọi vật ở trong đó" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "host" here means everything that fills the heavens and the earth (m1); a word for an army would mislead.

source.text: וַיְכַ֤ל אֱלֹהִים֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י מְלַאכְתּ֖וֹ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה וַיִּשְׁבֹּת֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י מִכָּל־מְלַאכְתּ֖וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָֽׂה׃

records.literal_gloss: And completed God on the day the seventh his work which he had done, and he rested on the day the seventh from all his work which he had done.

en.L: And on the seventh day God completed {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} work that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had done, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rested on the seventh day from all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} work that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had done.
en.B: On the seventh day God brought to an end the work {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had been doing, and on the seventh day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} stopped all the work {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had done.
en.R: When the seventh day came, God had finished {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} work. So on the seventh day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rested from all the work {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had been doing.

es.L: Y completó Dios en el día séptimo {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} obra que había hecho, y descansó en el día séptimo de toda {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} obra que había hecho.
es.B: El séptimo día Dios dio por terminada la obra que había estado haciendo, y en el séptimo día cesó todo el trabajo que había hecho.
es.R: Cuando llegó el séptimo día, Dios ya había terminado {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} obra. Así que el séptimo día descansó de todo el trabajo que había estado haciendo.

fr.L: Et Dieu termina, le septième jour, {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} ouvrage qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait fait, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} se reposa, le septième jour, de tout {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} ouvrage qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait fait.
fr.B: Le septième jour, Dieu mit un terme à l’ouvrage qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait fait, et ce septième jour-là {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} cessa tout l’ouvrage qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait accompli.
fr.R: Quand le septième jour est arrivé, Dieu avait fini {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} travail. Alors, le septième jour, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} s’est reposé de tout le travail qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait fait.

sw.L: Na siku ya saba Mungu akaikamilisha kazi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} aliyokuwa ameifanya, akapumzika siku ya saba kutoka kazi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} yote aliyokuwa ameifanya.
sw.B: Siku ya saba Mungu akaifikisha mwisho kazi aliyokuwa akiifanya, na siku hiyo ya saba akaacha kazi yote aliyokuwa ameifanya.
sw.R: Siku ya saba ilipofika, Mungu alikuwa amemaliza kazi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. Basi siku ya saba akapumzika baada ya kazi yote aliyokuwa akiifanya.

vi.L: Và vào ngày thứ bảy Đức Chúa Trời hoàn tất công việc của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} mà {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã làm, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nghỉ vào ngày thứ bảy khỏi mọi công việc của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} mà {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã làm.
vi.B: Đến ngày thứ bảy, Đức Chúa Trời kết thúc công việc {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã làm, và vào ngày thứ bảy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ngừng mọi công việc {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã làm.
vi.R: Khi ngày thứ bảy đến, Đức Chúa Trời đã làm xong công việc của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Vì vậy vào ngày thứ bảy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nghỉ mọi công việc {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã làm.

ko.L: 그리고 하나님께서 일곱째 날에 자신이 하신 일을 다 마치시고, 일곱째 날에 자신이 하신 모든 일을 쉬셨다.
ko.B: 일곱째 날에 하나님께서는 하시던 일을 끝내시고, 일곱째 날에 하시던 모든 일을 그치셨다.
ko.R: 일곱째 날이 되었을 때 하나님께서는 하시던 일을 다 마치셨다. 그래서 일곱째 날에는 하시던 모든 일을 멈추고 쉬셨다.

decisions.choice: completed on the seventh day: the seventh day is the end of the work, not more work
alternatives: God still did some work on the seventh day
decisions.reason: Read on its own, the first half could suggest that God was still working on the seventh day. The second half says what completing meant: on that day God rested. Finishing the work and ceasing from it are one act, and the seventh day is the completion of the week.

decisions.choice: on the seventh day, as in the Hebrew text
alternatives: on the sixth day (Samaritan Pentateuch, Septuagint, Syriac)
decisions.reason: The Samaritan Pentateuch, the Septuagint and the Syriac read "on the sixth day", probably so as not to suggest that God worked on the seventh. The Hebrew text, the harder reading, is followed here (m1).

decisions.choice: rested: stopped, ceased from work
decisions.reason: The verb means to stop or cease, and the word Sabbath comes from it. God does not rest because he is tired (Isaiah 40:28); he stops because the work is complete. Exodus 20:11 and 31:17 make this the pattern for Israel's Sabbath.

decisions.choice: work: a task, especially skilled work
decisions.reason: The word is used for skilled work such as the making of the tabernacle (Exodus 36:1-2), and for the work that is not to be done on the Sabbath (Exodus 20:9-10).

decisions.choice: brought to an end ... stopped
decisions.reason: Balanced says "brought to an end" and "stopped" so that the sentence does not seem to say that God worked on the seventh day (m1, m3). Literal keeps "completed" and "rested", and Readable says "had finished" and "rested".

decisions.choice: ouvrage (L, B); travail (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is used for skilled work such as the making of the tabernacle (m4). "Ouvrage" is French for a piece of skilled work and the thing made; Readable says "travail", the everyday word, as the English says "work".

decisions.choice: akapumzika (L, R); akaacha (B)
decisions.reason: The verb means to stop or cease (m3). "Kupumzika" is the ordinary word for resting from work; Balanced says "akaacha", "he stopped", as the English Balanced says "stopped" (r-en-1). "Kustarehe" suggests relaxing at ease.

decisions.choice: "자신이 하신 모든 일을 쉬셨다", as Hebrews 4:4 quotes this verse in Korean ("그분의 모든 일을 쉬셨다")
decisions.reason: The Korean Hebrews quotes this sentence; Literal uses the same verb "쉬다" with the work as its object, so the quotation and its source sound alike. Balanced says "그치셨다", stopped, as the English Balanced says "stopped" (meaning decision m3).

source.text: וַיְבָ֤רֶךְ אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶת־י֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י וַיְקַדֵּ֖שׁ אֹת֑וֹ כִּ֣י ב֤וֹ שָׁבַת֙ מִכָּל־מְלַאכְתּ֔וֹ אֲשֶׁר־בָּרָ֥א אֱלֹהִ֖ים לַעֲשֽׂוֹת׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And blessed God the day the seventh and made holy it, because on it he rested from all his work which created God to make.

en.L: And God blessed the seventh day and made it holy, because on it {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rested from all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} work that God had created to make.
en.B: God blessed the seventh day and set it apart as holy, since on that day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rested from all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} work, all that God had created and made.
en.R: God blessed the seventh day and made it a holy day. On that day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rested from all the work {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had done in creating the world.

es.L: Y bendijo Dios el día séptimo y lo santificó, porque en él descansó de toda {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} obra que Dios había creado para hacer.
es.B: Dios bendijo el séptimo día y lo apartó como santo, porque ese día descansó de toda {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} obra, de todo lo que había creado y hecho.
es.R: Dios bendijo el séptimo día y lo hizo un día santo. Ese día descansó de todo el trabajo que había hecho al crear el mundo.

fr.L: Et Dieu bénit le septième jour et le rendit saint, car en lui {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} se reposa de tout {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} ouvrage que Dieu avait créé pour faire.
fr.B: Dieu bénit le septième jour et le mit à part comme saint, puisque ce jour-là {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} se reposa de tout {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} ouvrage, de tout ce que Dieu avait créé et fait.
fr.R: Dieu a béni le septième jour et en a fait un jour saint. Ce jour-là, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} s’est reposé de tout le travail qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait fait en créant le monde.

sw.L: Na Mungu akaibariki siku ya saba na kuifanya takatifu, kwa sababu katika siku hiyo alipumzika kutoka kazi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} yote ambayo Mungu aliiumba ili kuifanya.
sw.B: Mungu akaibariki siku ya saba na kuitenga kuwa takatifu, kwa kuwa siku hiyo alipumzika baada ya kazi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} yote, yote ambayo Mungu aliyaumba na kuyafanya.
sw.R: Mungu akaibariki siku ya saba na kuifanya siku takatifu. Siku hiyo alipumzika baada ya kazi yote aliyoifanya alipoumba ulimwengu.

vi.L: Và Đức Chúa Trời ban phước cho ngày thứ bảy và làm cho nó nên thánh, vì trong ngày ấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nghỉ khỏi mọi công việc của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} mà Đức Chúa Trời đã sáng tạo để làm.
vi.B: Đức Chúa Trời ban phước cho ngày thứ bảy và biệt riêng ngày ấy ra thánh, vì trong ngày ấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nghỉ mọi công việc của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, tức là mọi điều Đức Chúa Trời đã sáng tạo và làm ra.
vi.R: Đức Chúa Trời ban phước cho ngày thứ bảy và làm cho ngày ấy thành một ngày thánh. Trong ngày ấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nghỉ mọi công việc {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã làm khi sáng tạo thế giới.

ko.L: 그리고 하나님께서 일곱째 날에 복을 주시고 그날을 거룩하게 하셨다. 그날에 하나님께서 창조하여 만드신 자신의 모든 일을 쉬셨기 때문이다.
ko.B: 하나님께서 일곱째 날에 복을 주시고, 그날을 거룩한 날로 구별하셨다. 그날에 하나님께서 창조하시고 만드신 모든 일을 마치고 쉬셨기 때문이다.
ko.R: 하나님께서 일곱째 날에 복을 주시고, 그날을 거룩한 날로 삼으셨다. 그날에 하나님께서 세상을 창조하시던 모든 일을 멈추고 쉬셨기 때문이다.

decisions.choice: made holy: set apart as belonging to God
decisions.reason: To make something holy is to set it apart for God. The first thing in the Bible that God makes holy is a day, not a place or an object. Israel is later told to keep the Sabbath holy for this reason (Exodus 20:8-11).

decisions.choice: which God created to make: all the work God did in creating
alternatives: which God created so that it would go on making
decisions.reason: The words "created" and "to make" are joined to sum up the whole of God's work. The phrase closes the account with both of its main verbs: "create" (verses 1, 21, 27) and "make" (verses 7, 16, 25, 31).

decisions.choice: the seventh day has no evening and morning
decisions.reason: Each of the six days ends with "there was evening and there was morning". The seventh does not: the account ends with the day God blessed and made holy. Hebrews 4:3-10 draws on this to speak of God's rest as still open to his people.

decisions.choice: that God had created to make
alternatives: that God had created and made
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew "created to make" (m2); Balanced says "created and made".

decisions.choice: set it apart as holy
decisions.reason: Balanced adds "set apart" to say what "holy" means (m1).

decisions.choice: le rendit saint (L); le mit à part comme saint (B); en a fait un jour saint (R)
decisions.reason: "Saint" is the word for holy throughout the Pentateuch. "Sanctifier" is the traditional verb but now belongs to church language; French says the same with "saint" itself, and Balanced adds "mettre à part", as the English does (r-en-2, m1).

decisions.choice: "làm cho nên thánh" (L), "biệt riêng ra thánh" (B), "làm cho thành một ngày thánh" (R)
decisions.reason: To make holy is to set apart as belonging to God (m1); Balanced says it in those words, as the English Balanced does.
